Chapter Three: Living Under Surveillance and the Weight of Loyalty.
Imagine living in a place where trust isn’t just rare—it’s almost impossible. Every connection you have, every word you speak, is shaped by a quiet, careful caution. The state's presence isn't just felt through cameras or informants—it's woven into daily life, touching every home, every friendship, every hushed conversation.
Picture a family sitting down to dinner. Their voices are soft, every sentence measured. The kids? They already know not to ask too many questions, and the parents? They pick their words with extra care. Step outside, and you’ll see neighbors exchanging polite greetings—but nobody lingers. Why? Because everyone’s aware: a single careless remark could echo far beyond that moment.
It’s no different at work. Sure, coworkers share stories or laughter, but there’s always a sense that someone might be listening. Loyalty? It’s everything. But here’s the catch—it’s also risky. If you’re seen as disloyal, you don’t just put yourself in danger, but your family, your friends, even distant relatives could pay the price.
The system is built to keep everyone just a little bit nervous. Regular self-criticism sessions force people to confess—sometimes real things, sometimes thoughts they barely had. It’s supposed to reinforce loyalty, but what it really does is make everyone suspicious of each other. Trust becomes a guessing game, and most folks learn to hide their true feelings—even from themselves.
Now, if you’re lucky enough to have some privileges, the pressure only ramps up. The perks are real: better food, safer homes, maybe even a taste of security. But every step up is both a reward and a warning—because the higher you go, the farther you have to fall.
And all it takes is one tiny mistake—a lost document, a misunderstood joke. Suddenly, everything feels like it’s about to unravel. Fear hits hard. Friends keep their distance, colleagues won’t meet your eyes, and that sense of being completely alone? It grows fast. In this world, even innocence can’t always save you from suspicion.
That’s the real weight of loyalty. It shapes every choice, every thought. People start policing their own minds, trying to guess what might seem dangerous or rebellious. Over time, the line between what you truly believe and what you say just to survive? It starts to blur, until you’re not even sure where one ends and the other begins.
But even here, small moments of courage and kindness break through. Maybe a friend quietly offers support, or a neighbor risks sharing a secret. Those moments are rare, but they remind us—humanity doesn’t just disappear, even under the harshest conditions.
Still, the constant surveillance wears people down. It chips away at your sense of self, and the urge for freedom grows stronger. Some choose to conform even more, trying to fit the mold the state demands. But for others, that quiet longing for something more? It just can’t be ignored.
